title: No Signs of AI Payoff Outside the Tech Sector
date_basis: Publisher-displayed article date and author block.
summary: Uses aggregate corporate and productivity indicators to argue that a broad financial payoff is not evident. Useful as a macro-level challenge, not identification of zero AI returns.
limitations: Mag 7 versus the remaining S&P constituents is not a clean technology/non-technology comparison. No no-AI counterfactual, adoption-level design or causal ROI estimate is supplied. Raw inputs were not reconstructed; Apollo has commercial interests. Charts are not redistributed.

verification.basis: Article text, byline, date, chart captions and source/disclosure notes inspected. Chart series were not digitized or independently reconstructed.

title: OpenAI and Anthropic cut their LLM prices by up to 80% within a few months. Why?
date_basis: Publisher-displayed publication date and author biography.
summary: Explains advertised model-price reductions through competition and caching. Useful for distinguishing token rates, workload costs and aggregate spending; market and profitability explanations remain hypotheses.
limitations: Selected prices and practitioner experience, not a causal market study. Token-volume shares are not dollar shares. Future prices, switching costs and supplier margins cannot be inferred from provider counts or current rate cards. Not every historical announcement was independently checked.

verification.basis: Full blog article including pricing timeline and speculative explanations inspected. Selected price fields cross-checked against official Anthropic and OpenAI announcements; Vercel's linked methodology inspected separately.

title: A Mathematician Reads the AI Future
date_basis: Local Chrome publisher heading, Steven Strogatz byline and timestamp: 25 October 2026, 8 AM ET.
summary: Strogatz distinguishes obtaining mathematical results from understanding them and from the human experience of discovery. Alongside anxiety about research careers and training, he describes Townsend's constructive program of AI-assisted problem solving, question selection, theory building and interpretation. Reported reactions illustrate contested purposes of mathematical work, not a consensus or a measured learning effect.
limitations: Expert essay with selected first-person accounts, not a representative survey, causal study or proof verification. Numerical breakthrough announcements and reported problem solutions are not independently validated by reading this essay. Cornell events and correspondence remain attributed reporting; the pure/applied distinction is an interpretive simplification, not an established taxonomy of attitudes. Concerns about training and careers are not measured long-run outcomes. A user-supplied Safari printout enabled full-text reading; the publisher page may remain subscription-restricted.

verification.basis: Complete essay read in a user-supplied 10-page Safari PDF printout, including ending and author biography. Printed title, Steven Strogatz byline, timestamp and canonical URL match the prior local Chrome identity inspection. Full-text appraisal does not independently verify mathematical proofs, numerical announcements or reported correspondence. Historical Chrome preview scope is preserved separately.

document_verification.filename: A Mathematician Reads the AI Future - The Atlantic.pdf
document_verification.scope: Full essay: identity and date on page 1, body on pages 2-8, author biography on page 9; page 10 contains only print headers/footers. PDF metadata identifies the user as print creator, not article author. No mathematical proof independently checked.

title: AI use leads UC Berkeley math professor to see ‘no point’ in grading homework
date_basis: Article byline and 23 October date in Chrome, distinguished from the site's current-day masthead.
summary: Reports Richard Borcherds's shift from correctness-based homework marking to completion credit, alongside concerns about AI and accounts of course-level policy discretion.
limitations: One reported interview, not a learning experiment or evidence that Berkeley abolished homework grading. Completion credit remains. Predictions about future mathematicians and claims about detector suitability are attributed statements, not independently established outcomes.

verification.basis: Full rendered article, Audrey Baime byline, date and distinction between Borcherds's remarks and Anne Marie Richard's reported institutional comments inspected in native local Chrome. Photo credit not substituted for author.

title: AI reshapes India's IT services sector contracts as clients demand more for less
date_basis: Date of the inspected Reuters syndication in The Star: 21 August 2026, with the same dateline. Original supplied Reuters URL contains 20 August; MarketScreener displays a 20 August US-edition timestamp. Citation dates the inspected edition rather than inferring a contradiction.
summary: Reports pricing pressure, outcome-linked fees, insourcing and shorter contracts in Indian IT services. It motivates separating productivity gains from the share of benefits captured by suppliers.
limitations: Interviews and partly anonymous contract accounts, not audited customer savings or a causal industry estimate. Requested discounts and promised future gains are not realized results. One reported TCS percentage concerns its business-services segment, not all contracts. Syndications are one report, not independent confirmations.

verification.basis: Reuters-attributed syndications inspected in The Star and MarketScreener, including byline, date, contract discussion and executive claims. Original Reuters host was inaccessible; private contract terms and corporate forecasts were not audited.

title: Claude Opus 5.5
date_basis: Dated official release page and its pricing table.
summary: Primary snapshot of advertised Opus 5.5 token rates and their comparison with Opus 5. Used for price verification, not independent validation of vendor performance claims.
limitations: Advertised API rates do not establish actual enterprise invoices, provider margins, future prices or total project cost. Workload savings and capability comparisons on the page are vendor estimates, not findings replicated by this review.

pricing_snapshot.scope: Standard pricing table, not fast-mode rates or a subscription quota.

verification.basis: Official page date, cost discussion and pricing table inspected. Benchmark scores, safety evaluations and advertised task savings were not independently appraised.

title: Open weight takes 71.5% of tokens and 23% of spend
date_basis: Publisher author block and 15 October 2026 date; measurement period extends through September 2026.
summary: Within one gateway, reported average token prices fall while estimated aggregate spending grows. Its methodology separates token volume from list-price-imputed spending.
limitations: Not a representative sample of all AI users. Spending is estimated using published prices, not actual bills; model mix, changing definitions and revised history affect comparisons. Counts combine several token categories. This does not establish quality-adjusted task savings or ROI.

verification.basis: Article findings, author/date block and About this report measurement notes inspected. Underlying private traffic not independently analyzed; public-data downloads not reconstructed.

title: “We should be more ambitious with the software we build”
date_basis: Publisher RSS entry at https://danluu.com/atom.xml: pubDate Sat, 24 Oct 2026 00:00:00 +0000; entry link and guid match the essay. The endpoint contains RSS XML, despite its filename.
summary: Argues that AI expands feasible software projects, not merely task speed; pairs practical examples with verification constraints and Kreinin's caution about excessive ambition.
limitations: Selected practitioner accounts, not a controlled effect. The author discloses limited benchmarking. Personal-tool usability does not establish production readiness; quoted discussion is not a separate study. Model, speed and cost claims are not independently reproduced here.

verification.basis: Full essay, appendices, counterargument and caveats inspected; exact publication date matched in publisher RSS using a structured XML parser. Two linked PostgreSQL reports and their replies were inspected separately, without executing their reproducers.

title: Re: BUG #19597: getQuadrant: impossible case is reachable
date_basis: Official PostgreSQL mailing-list archive: message date and Message-ID.
summary: Tiwari reports reproducing Malis's SP-GiST numerical-boundary bug on upstream master and proposes a patch. This supports the existence of a concrete validation outcome, not a general AI effect.
limitations: We read the messages but did not run the reproducer, inspect the attachment or establish a merged fix. Neither message isolates AI's causal contribution or validates pgrust's overall compatibility, performance or production readiness.

verification.basis: Official archive metadata, original report and full reply inspected; quoted report distinguished from the reply author's reproduction statement. No code executed.
